title: Radioactive decay and half-life
summary: With a 10-year half-life, N = 100 · 0.5^(t/10): half remains after every 10 years, and on a log axis the decay is a straight line.

beats.title: Atoms decay
beats.narration: Start with 100 atoms. The number left falls quickly at first, then more and more slowly.

beats.title: Half of them in 10 years
beats.narration: Draw a line at 50, half the start. The curve crosses it at t = 10 years: that is the half-life.

beats.title: And half again
beats.narration: Ten years later, half of the 50 is left: 25. Every half-life halves what remains.

beats.title: A straight line on a log axis
beats.narration: Plot the same numbers on a logarithmic axis and the curve becomes a straight line: equal steps in time, equal factors in N.
